characters: Afia: a fourteen-year-old JHS 3 student holding a school tablet, sharp on data ethics and statistics.
Bature: her classmate holding a protractor, compass, and tally sheet beside cassava leaves.
Mawuli: their classmate wearing a clean agro-processing apron beside stainless-steel gari-roasting equipment.
Madam Adomako: the JHS Computing and Artificial Intelligence club mentor.

narrationPlan.voice: Inquisitive teen voices for Afia, Bature, and Mawuli; warm, insightful Computing teacher voice for Madam Adomako
narrationPlan.pace: Curious, investigative, and clear (about 125 words per minute)
notes: Read dialogue with distinct, natural voices for each JHS student and teacher.
Pause for two seconds at each comprehension check so learners can calculate or reason first.
Pronounce spreadsheet formulas, geometric terms, and security acronyms clearly and unhurriedly.

music: Warm acoustic highlife guitar blended with gentle kalimba pulses evoking curiosity and discovery (placeholder)
culturalNotes: Proposed CCP curriculum links: Computing (B8.4.4.1 / B9.4.4.1 AI & Machine Learning bias), Mathematics (B7.4.1.1 / B8.4.1.1 Frequency Tables & Pie Charts), and Career Technology (B8.2.4.1 Food Commodities—cassava to gari value chain).
BECE Maths Guardrail: Explicitly contrasts Percentage (25%) with Pie-Chart Sector Angle (90°).
reviewQuestions: Is the language right for the stated JHS age band (Basic 7 to Basic 9) and BECE conceptual level?

teacherGuide.overview: Demystifies Artificial Intelligence for Ghanaian JHS students—connecting Machine Learning training bias, BECE pie-chart construction, unbiased sampling, and hygienic local cassava-to-gari agro-processing.
learningGoals: Explain how Machine Learning models learn from training data and why bias occurs.
Construct a frequency table and calculate exact pie-chart sector angles summing to 360°.
Describe the food-processing stages that make cassava safe as fortified gari.

beforeReading: Ask: If a voice assistant is trained only on British accents, why might it struggle with Ghanaian town names?
whileReading: Pause on Page 4: Have every learner verify 27/180 × 360° = 54° without a calculator.
afterReading: Survey classmates on favourite Ghanaian staples and construct an accurate pie chart.
discussion: Why should farmers treat AI predictions as a helpful second opinion rather than unquestionable truth?
reflection: Why is it vital for young Ghanaians to become creators and trainers of AI technologies?

mathsExtension.task: On 36 held-out test photos, the AI classified 33 correctly. Express test accuracy as a percentage to 1 decimal place.

support: Teach unit degree shortcut: when Total = 180, 1 item = 360° ÷ 180 = 2°.
stretch: Explore image classification using classroom objects and note changes with lighting.
